This file is created to document the various types of issues or failures which I will face during my devops Journey.

I was trying to commit my changes to remote but when I tried to push the changes to origin main, git gave the error,
large files being commited, refer a link to store large files,

RCA - on debugging I found that I was committing terraform provider files which was 700 mmb and git doesn't allow to commit such big files
So I had to create .gitignore file which was not there previously and then I tried commiting again.

# Terraform generated files and local state
**/.terraform/
**/*.tfstate
**/*.tfstate.*
**/*.tfvars
mentioned these file in gitignore.

but still I was facing issues that the index already has the changes and git was giving me that same error.

-- had to remove the already tracked files from Git's index.
I added .gitignore after I ran the commit, so that large file commit was still there in Git's Index which needs to be removed.

-- Rewrite the commit hostiry to erase the large files from every past commit.
even though I stopped tracking those large files, the old commits stll has the blobs and caused the push to fail.

commands to perform above steps :
# 1. Stop tracking the Terraform-generated files (keep them on disk)
git rm -r --cached \
  SETUP/terraform-aws-instances/.terraform \
  SETUP/terraform-aws-instances/terraform.tfstate \
  SETUP/terraform-aws-instances/terraform.tfstate.backup \
  SETUP/terraform-aws-instances/terraform.tfvars

# Stage the .gitignore file (created earlier) so the ignore rules are committed
git add .gitignore

# 2. Rewrite history to remove those files from every commit on main
git filter-branch --force --index-filter '
  git rm -r --cached --ignore-unmatch \
    SETUP/terraform-aws-instances/.terraform \
    SETUP/terraform-aws-instances/terraform.tfstate \
    SETUP/terraform-aws-instances/terraform.tfstate.backup \
    SETUP/terraform-aws-instances/terraform.tfvars
' --prune-empty --tag-name-filter cat -- main

# (Optional) Verify the large objects are no longer reachable
git rev-list --objects main | grep -E 'terraform-provider-aws|\.terraform|terraform\.tfstate|terraform\.tfvars' || echo "No large files found in history"

# Finally, push the cleaned history (requires force‑with‑lease because history changed)
git push --force-with-lease origin main

--force-with-lease is a safer alternative to --force when pushing to a remote branch.

What it does: It allows you to overwrite the remote branch with your local history only if the 
remote branch is exactly what you expect (i.e., no one else has pushed new commits since you last 
fetched).

How it works: Git checks the current tip of the remote branch against the value you have stored 
locally (your “lease”). If they match, the push proceeds; if they don’t (meaning someone else has 
pushed in the meantime), the push is rejected and you must fetch, re‑base/merge, and try again.
Why use it: It prevents you from accidentally overwriting somebody else’s work that you haven’t 
seen yet, while still letting you rewrite history when you know the remote hasn’t changed.
